title: Leaseholder fairness router and predictive overcommit mitigation
creator: Ayesha Gupta
description: Design and implement a leaseholder-based routing layer for dedicated fleets that enforces short-term throughput guarantees while using predictive forecasts to detect imminent overcommit and apply proportional, tenant-aware shedding. The feature combines lightweight per-tenant leases (time-bound credits) with a centralized short-term arbiter that decides spillback, soft-degrade actions, and model-variant fallbacks before hard rejections. Goals: keep high-priority SLAs stable during bursts, reduce tail latency for guaranteed tenants, and minimize customer-visible 429s by proactively demoting or rerouting low-impact work.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant baseline throughput guarantees enforced at ingress for at least 95% of minutes in a 7-day canary window
Predictive overcommit detector reduces hard 429s by >= 30% vs baseline during synthetic surge tests
Graceful fallback actions implemented: model-variant demotion, token-budgeted response truncation, and Retry-After semantics
Canary rollout behind feature-flag; canary fleet shows no >5% increase in P99 latency for guaranteed tenants
Instrumentation and dashboards available: per-tenant lease utilization, predicted vs observed load delta, shed-rate, and SLA violations
tasks: Define lease token format and lifecycle (TTL, refill rate, borrow window) - spec doc
Implement ingress lease check and local soft-queue with backpressure signals
Build predictive overcommit detector module (ML-lite time-series forecast + heuristic fallback)
Create centralized short-term arbiter that aggregates headroom and issues spillback decisions
Integrate shedding actions: model-variant route, response truncation, or 429 with Retry-After
Add telemetry, dashboards, and alerts (Grafana + PagerDuty runbook update)
Canary rollout to dedicated fleets, collect metrics, iterate on thresholds
discussion: 2026-03-10 - Ayesha G: Initial proposal posted. Rationale: current hard-shedding is noisy during multi-tenant bursts; we need preemptive measures to preserve contracted throughput for reserved customers.

2026-03-11 - Marcus Lee (PM): Please ensure contract/legal team reviewed the semantics of 'guarantee' vs 'best-effort' for reserved SKUs. We should include explicit wording in the customer-facing docs and billing triggers for sustained shedding.

2026-03-11 - Nina Park (Eng): Prototype idea: lease tokens are cheap integers attached to API keys; local agents can borrow from a 1s borrow window to smooth microbursts. Central arbiter reconciles every 2s. Concern: cross-region clock skew causes transient negative leases—proposal to use hybrid logical timestamps for reconciliation.

2026-03-11 - Rahul Singh (Security): Security review required for any token encoding touching customer IDs. Suggest HMAC with rotating signing key (KMS) and audit log entries for all fallback decisions. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-12 - Design decision: We will avoid per-request heavy crypto; leases will be opaque signed tokens with short TTL (<=30s). Central arbiter keeps canonical counts; local agents trust signed token + last-sync delta. This favors availability and low p99 latency.

2026-03-12 - Trade-offs: Centralized arbiter simplifies global fairness but is a potential availability hotspot. Mitigation: N replicas with leaderless reconciliation and circuit-breaker that switches to best-effort demotion in degraded mode.
2026-03-12 - QA note: Need synthetic load harness that can replay tenant-mix from production traces (use workload-sim repo: github.com/redwood-inference/workload-sim/tree/lease-exp)

runbook_and_rollout: Feature-flagged rollout: start with one low-traffic pool (canary), monitor lease_utilization and shed_rate for 72h
If canary metrics stable, expand to 10% fleet over 1 week. If SLA regressions >5% for guaranteed tenants, rollback flag immediately
Runbook page: https://runbook.redwood.ai/lease-router (includes mitigation steps: force-demote, disable-predictor, clear-lease-cache)
